title: Introduce profile entropy normalizer and changelog snippet generator
author: Evelyn Chen
description:
Motivation: onboarding incoming model profiles exhibits noisy and inconsistent metadata keys (latency_ms vs p50_ms, throughput vs tokens/s), variable histogram bucket schemas, and transitive metadata noise from third-party exports. That noise prevents reliable changelog snippets and causes churn in profile diffs used by release automation.

This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: 1) a Profile Entropy Normalizer that canonicalizes field names, normalizes metric units and histogram buckets, and computes a per-profile "entropy" signal to surface noisy or under-sampled profiles; and 2) a Changelog Snippet Generator that consumes normalized profiles + diffs and emits compact, human-readable changelog fragments suitable for the release assembler and autosuggest UI.

What changed (high level): canonical field map and unit conversion rules for latency/throughput/size, histogram bucket alignment and merge heuristics, a lightweight entropy estimator (shannon-with-smoothing) that flags profiles below sampling thresholds, a deterministic normalization pipeline (idempotent) to ensure stable diffs, and a templated snippet generator that emits a 1-2 sentence summary with top 3 metric deltas and a sample delta table when available. The generator also tags snippets with affinity hints (gpu/cpu/quantized) to feed release categorization.

Backward compatibility and rollout: the normalizer runs as an opt-in preprocessing hook for onboarded profiles (controlled via onboarding config). For the hosted ingestion pipeline we add an interim compatibility toggle that keeps raw profile payloads in the provenance ledger while normalizer outputs are stored as derived profiles. Migration docs and a migration script are included to backfill existing profiles in a staged rollout.

Testing and validation: unit tests for field mapping and unit conversion, fuzzy tests for histogram merging across bucket schemas, integration test for the changelog snippet template outputs (English and minimal i18n-safe escaping), and a smoke backfill run against a 5k sample set to validate entropy distributions. CI runs included a targeted sampling harness that compares normalized diffs against existing release assembler inputs to ensure no regressions in release candidate generation.

Why this is unique: instead of only improving changelog text generation, this PR treats input quality as a first-class problem (profile entropy) and provides deterministic normalization so downstream changelog automation and A/B rollout decisions see stable, low-noise signals.

Related: ENG-1478 (profile stabilizer), ENG-1499 (release automation quality), SUP-3241 (customer-reported noisy onboarded profiles).

review_conversation: Priya Nair: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: include example of a canonicalized profile in the docs and ensure the entropy threshold is configurable per-customer.
Evelyn Chen: Added canonical profile example and made threshold honor onboarding config with sane defaults (see preprocess_hook).
Carlos Mendes: Histogram alignment looks reasonable. One nit: prefer explicit bucket merge policy names (e.g., 'align-by-centroid') vs booleans for readability.
Evelyn Chen: Renamed merge modes and added short comments and test case for align-by-centroid and align-by-boundaries.
Jordan Patel: Integration tests pass for a 5k-sample backfill; approving with the expectation we monitor entropy spike metrics post-rollout.
release_notes:
- Add deterministic profile normalizer that canonicalizes metrics and histogram buckets.
- Introduce profile entropy metric to flag low-sample/noisy profiles.
- Add changelog snippet generator that creates concise release blurbs from normalized diffs.
- Opt-in onboarding hook and backfill script for staged rollout.
